blocks.title: DHCP and ARP
items: DHCP DORA: Discover (broadcast), Offer, Request, Acknowledge. Renewal starts at 50% of the lease (T1), rebind at 87.5% (T2).
A DHCP relay (`ip helper-address`) forwards broadcasts to a server on another subnet.
ARP maps IPv4 address to MAC on the local segment; gratuitous ARP announces or detects duplicates.
APIPA 169.254.x.x on a client means no DHCP server answered.

sheets.title: IP addressing
sheets.blurb: Special ranges, classes, the subnet table, IPv6.

blocks.title: Subnetting in four steps
items: Block size = 256 minus the interesting octet of the mask (for example /26: 256 - 192 = 64).
Network = the multiple of the block size at or below the host's value in that octet.
Broadcast = next network address minus 1; usable range sits between network and broadcast.
Hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2. Subnets = 2^(borrowed bits). Need N hosts: smallest 2^h with 2^h - 2 >= N.

blocks.title: IPv6 address types
head: Type
Prefix
Notes
rows: Every interface; not routed; used by NDP and routing protocols
ff02::1 all nodes, ff02::2 all routers; no broadcast in IPv6

blocks.text: IPv6 is 128 bits written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits. Drop leading zeros in a group, and replace one run of all-zero groups with `::` (once only). Standard subnet is /64. SLAAC builds an address from the router's prefix plus an interface ID (EUI-64 or random); DHCPv6 can be stateful or stateless. NDP replaces ARP.

sheets.title: Switching, routing, WAN
sheets.blurb: VLANs, STP, routing protocols, NAT, VPN, QoS and topologies.

blocks.title: Switching facts
items: VLAN = broadcast domain. 802.1Q trunk adds a 4-byte tag; the native VLAN is sent untagged. Voice VLAN is separate from data.
STP (802.1D) blocks redundant links to prevent loops; RSTP (802.1w) converges faster. Root bridge = lowest bridge ID (priority 32768 by default, then MAC).
Port roles: root, designated, alternate/blocked. PortFast for edge ports; BPDU guard disables a port if a BPDU arrives.
Link aggregation: LACP (802.3ad) bundles links; PoE 802.3af 15.4 W, 802.3at 30 W, 802.3bt up to 90 W.
Port mirroring (SPAN) copies traffic to a monitoring port. Port security limits MAC addresses per port.

blocks.title: NAT, VPN and WAN
items: NAT translates private to public addresses. PAT (overload) shares one public IP using port numbers. Static NAT is one-to-one.
Site-to-site VPN joins networks; client VPN joins a single device. IPsec: AH (integrity), ESP (confidentiality + integrity); IKE negotiates keys.
Split tunnel sends only corporate traffic through the VPN; full tunnel sends everything.
WAN: MPLS (provider labels), metro Ethernet, broadband cable/DSL/fiber, satellite (high latency), cellular 4G/5G. SD-WAN steers traffic across links by policy.
QoS prioritizes traffic: classification and marking (DSCP), queuing, shaping, policing. Voice needs low latency, jitter and loss.

blocks.title: Topologies and architectures
items: Star (one central switch, most common), mesh (full or partial, redundancy), bus, ring, hub-and-spoke (WAN).
Three-tier: access, distribution, core. Collapsed core: distribution and core combined. Spine-leaf: data center, every leaf connects to every spine.
North-south traffic enters or leaves the data center; east-west moves between servers inside it.
Cloud: public, private, hybrid, community. IaaS, PaaS, SaaS. VPC, transit gateway, direct connect/ExpressRoute.

sheets.title: Troubleshooting
sheets.blurb: Method, commands, tools and common symptoms.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting method (CompTIA)
items: 1. Identify the problem (gather information, question users, duplicate it, check changes).
2. Establish a theory of probable cause (start simple; consider the OSI model).
3. Test the theory to determine the cause. If it fails, form a new theory or escalate.
4. Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects.
5. Implement the solution or escalate.
6. Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures.
7. Document findings, actions and outcomes.

blocks.title: Hardware tools
items: Cable tester: continuity and pinout. Toner and probe: find a cable in a bundle. TDR: distance to a copper break. OTDR: distance to a fiber break.
Loopback plug: tests a port. Wi-Fi analyzer: signal and channels. Protocol analyzer / packet sniffer: capture and decode traffic (Wireshark).
Crimper and punch-down tool for terminations; multimeter for voltage and continuity; optical power meter for fiber loss.
Pinouts: T568B is the common standard (orange pair first); a straight-through cable is the same standard on both ends, a crossover is T568A on one end and T568B on the other.

blocks.title: Security quick facts
items: CIA: confidentiality, integrity, availability. AAA: authentication, authorization, accounting. Zero trust: verify every request.
Common attacks: DoS/DDoS, on-path (MITM), ARP poisoning, DNS poisoning, VLAN hopping (double tagging, switch spoofing), rogue AP/DHCP, evil twin, phishing, ransomware.
Defences: ACLs, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, port security, 802.1X, VLAN hygiene (disable unused ports, change the native VLAN), patching, segmentation, MFA.
NAC checks device posture before granting access. Honeypots lure attackers. Screened subnet (DMZ) hosts public services.
